meta.source: Eskom GCCA 2025 (Oct 2023) for baseline connection capacity, plus NTCSA "GCCA 2025 Update: Integrating Congestion Curtailment Capacity" (31 Oct 2025) for the Western Cape and Eastern Cape.
meta.curtailment_capacity: The 1,180 MW (WC) and 400 MW (EC) unlocked by 4% congestion curtailment is available to WIND GENERATORS ONLY - the Oct 2025 document is titled and scoped for wind specifically. Solar and firm technologies remain at 0 MW in both provinces. NERSA approval runs 1 Apr 2025 - 31 Mar 2028 at a 4% cap (more restrictive than the 10% / 3,470 MW sought in the Jan 2024 addendum).
meta.timing_caveat: That wind capacity is a 2028 figure, not capacity available today: hosting capacity rises from 5,625 MW to 7,205 MW BY 2028, and depends on new infrastructure. 720 MW of the WC allocation sits at the planned Nuweveld / Galenia substations, which NTCSA states must be delivered as SELF-BUILD projects; the EC 400 MW depends on the planned Pembroke transformer.
meta.replaces: Headroom previously derived from this app's own corridor-utilisation search, which only knew about OPERATIONAL plant and so ignored the committed-but-unbuilt pipeline that actually depleted the Cape provinces. That gave 72,250 MW national solar headroom against a published ~20 GW, and thousands of MW in the four supply areas Eskom reports as zero.
meta.caveat: The six non-Cape figures date from Oct 2023 and have likely been drawn down since - NTCSA's project dashboard (Nov 2025) shows 15.2 GW of solar alone seeking connection. Treat them as an upper bound.
meta.note: GCCA capacity is connection capacity at transmission substations, not a per-technology allowance, so allocations draw from one shared regional pool - except the WC/EC curtailment capacity, which is ring-fenced to wind.
